ann_12.original: identity_biology ≈ 0.345·z(tgrade=III) + 0.321·z(tgrade=II) -0.316·z(progrec), coefficients per standardised input (rounded; off by up to 0.0012 on the training rows; the exact weights are in the analytical_formula evidence). This part is a sparse linear block of the log-risk: tumour grade (the two one-hot levels against grade I) and progesterone receptor level each have a direct edge, summed into one identity exit and passed unchanged to the output, so the part is additive on the log-hazard scale and multiplicative on the hazard. In hazard-ratio terms per clinical unit, holding the other inputs fixed: relative to a grade I tumour, the model multiplies the hazard by 1.96 for grade II and by 2.26 for grade III; each additional fmol/l of progesterone receptor multiplies it by 0.9984 (one SD of progesterone receptor: 0.73), a protective direction. Across the training patients the progesterone-receptor term spans a hazard ratio of 1.92 between its 95th and 5th percentile, the grade III term 2.26 and the grade II term 1.96. Self-probe (whole model; a constructed patient with progesterone receptor 29.5 fmol/l, 3 positive nodes and no hormone therapy, the remaining inputs at the typical values of each grade cell, which is harmless because fixing the four unconnected inputs moves 0 of 438 training predictions): the log-risk is -1.199 for grade I, -0.526 for grade II and -0.382 for grade III, a predicted five-year risk of 34%, 56% and 61%; the two gaps match the per-unit log-hazard ratios 0.673 and 0.817. Sweeping progesterone receptor from 0 to 300 fmol/l on the typical grade II patient lowers the log-risk from -0.479 to -0.964 (five-year risk 58% to 41%). In the training split the part's mean contribution to the log-risk is 0.261 for the 102 grade III patients, 0.039 for the 285 grade II patients and -0.741 for the 51 grade I patients (the three grade cells are exhaustive: 0 patients carry both one-hot levels). Switching the whole part off (exit fixed at its training mean) moves the predicted five-year risk by 9% on average over the 438 training rows and lowers the AUC against the event indicator from 0.6805 to 0.6675. Meaning (concept probe over the tabular library): the best single concept for the exit is a progesterone-receptor threshold, score 0.91 (AUC 0.95, R-squared 0.30); because the part sums three terms, one concept captures its direction and not its value, so the part is described by its formula rather than by a single clinical concept. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of grade and receptor level on the hazard, so this is not evidence that these effects are constant over follow-up.
ann_12.proposed: A higher progesterone receptor lowers the hazard steadily and a grade III tumour raises it.

ann_13.original: identity_nodal ≈ 0.293·z(pnodes), a single direct edge from the number of positive lymph nodes to an identity exit that is passed unchanged to the log-risk (rounded coefficient per standardised input, off by up to 0.0035 on the training rows; the exact weight is in the analytical_formula evidence). In hazard-ratio terms per clinical unit, holding the other inputs fixed: each additional positive lymph node multiplies the hazard by 1.051 (one SD of the node count: 1.34); the part is one linear edge, so the effect is log-linear in the node count across the training range, without a threshold or a plateau. Across the training patients the term spans a hazard ratio of 2.12 between its 95th and 5th percentile, and 1.92 between the 95th-percentile and the median patient. Self-probe (whole model, the typical patient: grade II, no hormone therapy, progesterone receptor 29.5 fmol/l): sweeping positive nodes from 1 to 29 raises the log-risk from -0.627 to 0.775 and the predicted five-year risk from 53% to 95%, the part's contribution rising from -0.211 to 1.191; going from one positive node to two moves the log-risk from -0.6266 to -0.5765, which is the per-node log-hazard ratio 0.0501. In the training split the 71 patients with ten or more positive nodes have a mean predicted five-year risk of 71% (73% had an event during follow-up), against 43% for the 234 patients with three or fewer (31% had an event); this part's mean contribution to the log-risk is 0.520 in the first group and -0.175 in the second. Switching the part off (exit fixed at its training mean) moves the predicted five-year risk by 6% on average over the 438 training rows (largest change 49%) and lowers the AUC against the event indicator from 0.6805 to 0.6258, the largest loss of the three parts. Meaning: the exit is the positive-node count itself, concept probe score 1.00 for the concept pnodes. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of nodal burden on the hazard, so this is not evidence that the effect is constant over follow-up.
ann_13.proposed: Each extra positive lymph node adds about the same to the hazard.

ann_14.original: identity_hormone ≈ -0.206·z(horTh=yes), a single direct edge from the hormonal-therapy indicator to an identity exit that is passed unchanged to the log-risk (rounded coefficient per standardised input, off by up to 0.00023 on the training rows; the exact weight is in the analytical_formula evidence). In hazard-ratio terms: holding the other inputs fixed, the model gives a patient who received hormonal therapy 0.653 times the hazard of a patient who did not (per SD of the indicator: 0.81); the part has one binary input, so this is a fixed offset on the log-hazard scale that does not depend on the other inputs, and it is an association the model learned from this cohort, not a treatment effect. Across the training patients the term spans a hazard ratio of 1.53 between its 95th and 5th percentile. Self-probe (whole model; a constructed grade II patient with progesterone receptor 29.5 fmol/l and 3 positive nodes, the remaining inputs at the typical values of each therapy cell, which is harmless because fixing the four unconnected inputs moves 0 of 438 training predictions): the log-risk is -0.952 with therapy and -0.526 without, a predicted five-year risk of 42% against 56%; the gap matches the per-unit log-hazard ratio -0.425, and the part's contribution is -0.265 with therapy against 0.160 without (the inputs are standardised, so the untreated level is a positive offset and the treated level a negative one; the difference between them is the effect). In the training split the 165 treated patients have a mean predicted five-year risk of 41% (37% had an event during follow-up) and this part contributes -0.265 to their log-risk; the 273 untreated patients have 55% (48% had an event) with a contribution of 0.160. Switching the part off (exit fixed at its training mean) moves the predicted five-year risk by 6% on average over the 438 training rows (largest change 10%) and lowers the AUC against the event indicator from 0.6805 to 0.6767, the smallest loss of the three parts. Meaning: the exit is the therapy indicator itself, concept probe score 1.00 for the concept horTh=yes. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of hormonal therapy on the hazard, so this is not evidence that the effect is constant over follow-up.

ann_15.original: The output is the Cox log-risk g(x) with an identity activation: g(x) = tumour_biology + nodal_burden + hormone_therapy + constant, an exact sum (each of the three identity exits enters the output with unit weight; the constant is the output bias, which carries no meaning because it is absorbed into the baseline hazard). The three parts therefore combine additively on the log-hazard scale, that is multiplicatively on the hazard, h(t|x) = h0(t)·exp(g(x)), with the five-year risk read off a Breslow baseline fitted on the training rows. The 5 terms at the output are all direct input edges routed through the three identity exits (0 direct input edges remain at the output itself), so the model is a sparse linear Cox model with the following hazard ratios per clinical unit, holding the other inputs fixed: grade II versus grade I 1.96, grade III versus grade I 2.26, each positive lymph node 1.051, each fmol/l of progesterone receptor 0.9984, hormonal therapy 0.653. The four remaining inputs, age, oestrogen receptor, menopausal status and tumour size, are unconnected entry nodes with zero effect: fixing all four at once changes 0 of the 438 training predictions (largest absolute change in five-year risk 0.0), and sweeping the typical patient across the training range of age leaves the log-risk at -0.5265 at both ends (-0.5265), of tumour size at -0.5265 and -0.5265, and of oestrogen receptor at -0.5265 and -0.5265 (menopausal status could not be swept by the probe tool, whose variable parser stops at the "=" in the input name; its effect is covered by the same node ablation, 0 of 438 predictions changed). Across the training patients the log-risk spans a hazard ratio of 5.82 between the 95th- and the 5th-percentile patient. Survival performance on the training split (n = 438, 191 events): Harrell's C 0.682, Uno's C 0.651, time-dependent AUC at one, three and five years 0.765, 0.731 and 0.707, integrated Brier score 0.132; five-year calibration over ten risk deciles: mean predicted risk 50% against a Kaplan-Meier observed 49%, largest decile gap 11%. Self-probe of the composition: switching all three parts off at once leaves the constant alone, so the typical patient's log-risk goes from -0.526 to -0.747, the output bias (five-year risk 56% to 48%), and the AUC against the event indicator falls from 0.6805 to 0.50, chance level; by single-part ablation the AUC losses rank nodal_burden (0.6258) above tumour_biology (0.6675) above hormone_therapy (0.6767). Function preservation: the identity-node refactoring reproduces the original network's log-risk to 4.4e-16 on the training rows. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of each term on the hazard, so this is not evidence that any effect is constant over follow-up.
ann_15.proposed: The hazard of recurrence or death is a sum of three parts (tumour biology, nodal burden, hormonal therapy); age, oestrogen receptor, menopausal status and tumour size are ignored.

lead.text: For a typical patient (a 53-year-old postmenopausal woman with 3 positive lymph nodes, a grade II tumour of 25 mm, a progesterone receptor of 30 fmol/l, an oestrogen receptor of 36 fmol/l and no hormonal therapy) the model predicts a 5-year risk of recurrence or death of about 56%; it adds up three parts, tumour biology, nodal burden and hormonal therapy, and reads no other input directly.

parts.name: cox_log_risk
parts.original_hypothesis: The output is the Cox log-risk g(x) with an identity activation: g(x) = tumour_biology + nodal_burden + hormone_therapy + constant, an exact sum (each of the three identity exits enters the output with unit weight; the constant is the output bias, which carries no meaning because it is absorbed into the baseline hazard). The three parts therefore combine additively on the log-hazard scale, that is multiplicatively on the hazard, h(t|x) = h0(t)·exp(g(x)), with the five-year risk read off a Breslow baseline fitted on the training rows. The 5 terms at the output are all direct input edges routed through the three identity exits (0 direct input edges remain at the output itself), so the model is a sparse linear Cox model with the following hazard ratios per clinical unit, holding the other inputs fixed: grade II versus grade I 1.96, grade III versus grade I 2.26, each positive lymph node 1.051, each fmol/l of progesterone receptor 0.9984, hormonal therapy 0.653. The four remaining inputs, age, oestrogen receptor, menopausal status and tumour size, are unconnected entry nodes with zero effect: fixing all four at once changes 0 of the 438 training predictions (largest absolute change in five-year risk 0.0), and sweeping the typical patient across the training range of age leaves the log-risk at -0.5265 at both ends (-0.5265), of tumour size at -0.5265 and -0.5265, and of oestrogen receptor at -0.5265 and -0.5265 (menopausal status could not be swept by the probe tool, whose variable parser stops at the "=" in the input name; its effect is covered by the same node ablation, 0 of 438 predictions changed). Across the training patients the log-risk spans a hazard ratio of 5.82 between the 95th- and the 5th-percentile patient. Survival performance on the training split (n = 438, 191 events): Harrell's C 0.682, Uno's C 0.651, time-dependent AUC at one, three and five years 0.765, 0.731 and 0.707, integrated Brier score 0.132; five-year calibration over ten risk deciles: mean predicted risk 50% against a Kaplan-Meier observed 49%, largest decile gap 11%. Self-probe of the composition: switching all three parts off at once leaves the constant alone, so the typical patient's log-risk goes from -0.526 to -0.747, the output bias (five-year risk 56% to 48%), and the AUC against the event indicator falls from 0.6805 to 0.50, chance level; by single-part ablation the AUC losses rank nodal_burden (0.6258) above tumour_biology (0.6675) above hormone_therapy (0.6767). Function preservation: the identity-node refactoring reproduces the original network's log-risk to 4.4e-16 on the training rows. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of each term on the hazard, so this is not evidence that any effect is constant over follow-up.

parts.name: tumour_biology
parts.original_hypothesis: identity_biology ≈ 0.345·z(tgrade=III) + 0.321·z(tgrade=II) -0.316·z(progrec), coefficients per standardised input (rounded; off by up to 0.0012 on the training rows; the exact weights are in the analytical_formula evidence). This part is a sparse linear block of the log-risk: tumour grade (the two one-hot levels against grade I) and progesterone receptor level each have a direct edge, summed into one identity exit and passed unchanged to the output, so the part is additive on the log-hazard scale and multiplicative on the hazard. In hazard-ratio terms per clinical unit, holding the other inputs fixed: relative to a grade I tumour, the model multiplies the hazard by 1.96 for grade II and by 2.26 for grade III; each additional fmol/l of progesterone receptor multiplies it by 0.9984 (one SD of progesterone receptor: 0.73), a protective direction. Across the training patients the progesterone-receptor term spans a hazard ratio of 1.92 between its 95th and 5th percentile, the grade III term 2.26 and the grade II term 1.96. Self-probe (whole model; a constructed patient with progesterone receptor 29.5 fmol/l, 3 positive nodes and no hormone therapy, the remaining inputs at the typical values of each grade cell, which is harmless because fixing the four unconnected inputs moves 0 of 438 training predictions): the log-risk is -1.199 for grade I, -0.526 for grade II and -0.382 for grade III, a predicted five-year risk of 34%, 56% and 61%; the two gaps match the per-unit log-hazard ratios 0.673 and 0.817. Sweeping progesterone receptor from 0 to 300 fmol/l on the typical grade II patient lowers the log-risk from -0.479 to -0.964 (five-year risk 58% to 41%). In the training split the part's mean contribution to the log-risk is 0.261 for the 102 grade III patients, 0.039 for the 285 grade II patients and -0.741 for the 51 grade I patients (the three grade cells are exhaustive: 0 patients carry both one-hot levels). Switching the whole part off (exit fixed at its training mean) moves the predicted five-year risk by 9% on average over the 438 training rows and lowers the AUC against the event indicator from 0.6805 to 0.6675. Meaning (concept probe over the tabular library): the best single concept for the exit is a progesterone-receptor threshold, score 0.91 (AUC 0.95, R-squared 0.30); because the part sums three terms, one concept captures its direction and not its value, so the part is described by its formula rather than by a single clinical concept. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of grade and receptor level on the hazard, so this is not evidence that these effects are constant over follow-up.

closed_form.rounding: weights and biases at 3 significant figures

parts.name: nodal_burden
parts.original_hypothesis: identity_nodal ≈ 0.293·z(pnodes), a single direct edge from the number of positive lymph nodes to an identity exit that is passed unchanged to the log-risk (rounded coefficient per standardised input, off by up to 0.0035 on the training rows; the exact weight is in the analytical_formula evidence). In hazard-ratio terms per clinical unit, holding the other inputs fixed: each additional positive lymph node multiplies the hazard by 1.051 (one SD of the node count: 1.34); the part is one linear edge, so the effect is log-linear in the node count across the training range, without a threshold or a plateau. Across the training patients the term spans a hazard ratio of 2.12 between its 95th and 5th percentile, and 1.92 between the 95th-percentile and the median patient. Self-probe (whole model, the typical patient: grade II, no hormone therapy, progesterone receptor 29.5 fmol/l): sweeping positive nodes from 1 to 29 raises the log-risk from -0.627 to 0.775 and the predicted five-year risk from 53% to 95%, the part's contribution rising from -0.211 to 1.191; going from one positive node to two moves the log-risk from -0.6266 to -0.5765, which is the per-node log-hazard ratio 0.0501. In the training split the 71 patients with ten or more positive nodes have a mean predicted five-year risk of 71% (73% had an event during follow-up), against 43% for the 234 patients with three or fewer (31% had an event); this part's mean contribution to the log-risk is 0.520 in the first group and -0.175 in the second. Switching the part off (exit fixed at its training mean) moves the predicted five-year risk by 6% on average over the 438 training rows (largest change 49%) and lowers the AUC against the event indicator from 0.6805 to 0.6258, the largest loss of the three parts. Meaning: the exit is the positive-node count itself, concept probe score 1.00 for the concept pnodes. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of nodal burden on the hazard, so this is not evidence that the effect is constant over follow-up.

closed_form.rounding: weights and biases at 3 significant figures

parts.name: hormone_therapy
parts.original_hypothesis: identity_hormone ≈ -0.206·z(horTh=yes), a single direct edge from the hormonal-therapy indicator to an identity exit that is passed unchanged to the log-risk (rounded coefficient per standardised input, off by up to 0.00023 on the training rows; the exact weight is in the analytical_formula evidence). In hazard-ratio terms: holding the other inputs fixed, the model gives a patient who received hormonal therapy 0.653 times the hazard of a patient who did not (per SD of the indicator: 0.81); the part has one binary input, so this is a fixed offset on the log-hazard scale that does not depend on the other inputs, and it is an association the model learned from this cohort, not a treatment effect. Across the training patients the term spans a hazard ratio of 1.53 between its 95th and 5th percentile. Self-probe (whole model; a constructed grade II patient with progesterone receptor 29.5 fmol/l and 3 positive nodes, the remaining inputs at the typical values of each therapy cell, which is harmless because fixing the four unconnected inputs moves 0 of 438 training predictions): the log-risk is -0.952 with therapy and -0.526 without, a predicted five-year risk of 42% against 56%; the gap matches the per-unit log-hazard ratio -0.425, and the part's contribution is -0.265 with therapy against 0.160 without (the inputs are standardised, so the untreated level is a positive offset and the treated level a negative one; the difference between them is the effect). In the training split the 165 treated patients have a mean predicted five-year risk of 41% (37% had an event during follow-up) and this part contributes -0.265 to their log-risk; the 273 untreated patients have 55% (48% had an event) with a contribution of 0.160. Switching the part off (exit fixed at its training mean) moves the predicted five-year risk by 6% on average over the 438 training rows (largest change 10%) and lowers the AUC against the event indicator from 0.6805 to 0.6767, the smallest loss of the three parts. Meaning: the exit is the therapy indicator itself, concept probe score 1.00 for the concept horTh=yes. Proportional-hazards caveat: the model's form is a time-constant multiplicative effect of hormonal therapy on the hazard, so this is not evidence that the effect is constant over follow-up.

ph_caveat: Each effect multiplies the hazard by the same amount at every point of follow-up, because the model has no way to represent an effect that changes with time (the proportional-hazards assumption); this is not evidence that the effect is constant over time.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log hazard ratio (the model's log-risk) for verification; the hazard ratio and the predicted risk by the horizon for the typical patient for wording

ann_12.text: Through this part, the model treats a higher progesterone receptor as clearly lowering the predicted 5-year risk of recurrence or death steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 58% at 0 fmol/l to about 42% at 295 fmol/l, a hazard ratio of about 0.62.

Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted 5-year risk of recurrence or death if the patient has tumour grade III (with tumour grade II at a tumour grade other than II, as in the data) (about 61%) than if the patient has a tumour grade other than III (about 56%), a hazard ratio of about 1.5 (on the training data only).

ann_13.text: Through this part, the model treats a higher number of positive lymph nodes as raising the predicted 5-year risk of recurrence or death steadily: for a typical patient, it goes from about 53% at 1 nodes to about 73% at 12 nodes, a hazard ratio of about 1.7 (on the training data only).

ann_14.text: Through this part, for a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted 5-year risk of recurrence or death if the patient has hormonal therapy (about 42%) than if the patient has no hormonal therapy (about 56%), a hazard ratio of about 0.65 (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a lower predicted 5-year risk of recurrence or death if the patient has hormonal therapy (about 42%) than if the patient has no hormonal therapy (about 56%), a hazard ratio of about 0.65 (on the training data only).

For a typical patient, the model gives a higher predicted 5-year risk of recurrence or death if the patient has tumour grade III (with tumour grade II at a tumour grade other than II, as in the data) (about 61%) than if the patient has a tumour grade other than III (about 56%), a hazard ratio of about 1.5 (on the training data only).
It ignores age, oestrogen receptor, postmenopausal status and tumour size.
